subject: Architecture
title: Bosco Verticale: A Forest on a Tower
description: Learn Bosco Verticale: A Forest on a Tower in one minute.

hook.text: Two residential towers in Milan hold 900 trees, 5,000 shrubs, and 11,000 plants on their balconies.

buildup.text: Bosco Verticale — 'Vertical Forest' — was designed by Stefano Boeri to bring nature into dense city life.

discovery.text: The plants filter dust, produce oxygen, and shade apartments — reducing air conditioning needs by 30%.

twist.text: Maintaining the trees requires 'flying gardeners' who rappel down the facade on ropes to prune branches.

climax.text: The concept is spreading — vertical forests are now planned in Nanjing, Utrecht, Cairo, and São Paulo.

punchline.text: They planted a forest on a skyscraper. Now cities want their own.

quiz.question: How are trees maintained on Bosco Verticale's balconies?
options: Gardeners rappel down the facade on ropes
Residents maintain their own trees with provided kits

details.summary: Bosco Verticale (Vertical Forest) in Milan hosts 900 trees, 5,000 shrubs, and 11,000 plants on its two residential towers. Designed by Stefano Boeri, the vegetation provides shade, produces oxygen, absorbs CO2 and dust, dampens noise.
details.whyItMatters: Bosco Verticale proved that dense urban development and biodiversity can coexist vertically. Its success launched a global movement of forested towers, demonstrating that high-rise living doesn't have to mean disconnection from nature.
takeaways: 900 trees and 11,000 plants grow on two residential towers in Milan
Vegetation provides shade, oxygen, carbon absorption, and habitat
It launched a global movement of vertical forest buildings

faq.question: How are the trees maintained on the towers?
faq.answer: Specialized arborists rappel down the facades for pruning and maintenance. An automated drip irrigation system waters each planter individually. Trees were pre-grown to withstand wind conditions at building height and tested in wind tunnels before installation.

faq.question: Has Bosco Verticale inspired similar projects?
faq.answer: Yes, extensively. Boeri's firm has designed vertical forests for cities including Nanjing, Eindhoven, Cairo, and Tirana. Other architects have proposed similar concepts worldwide. The idea of integrating significant vegetation into high-rise buildings has become a mainstream architectural trend.
